methodology_note: Study units derived from Toronto Notes SOURCE STRUCTURE (toc_inventory.json), not from medical memory. Generic structural headings (organizational section umbrellas with no independent content) are NOT converted into standalone units - see organizational_header_nodes below for how each is accounted for.
page_range_inheritance_note: Unlike some other chapters' study_units.json, most study units here use EXACT_SECTION/EXACT_TOPIC page_mapping_precision rather than SECTION_INHERITED, because chapter A's derivation involved reading the chapter's raw OCR pages directly (derived/toronto-notes-2025/ocr/pages/0055.json through 0090.json) rather than relying solely on toc_inventory.json's flat 3-level structure. Where a topic's exact body-heading position was not independently re-verified (SU-A-17, SU-A-25), SECTION_INHERITED/MEDIUM confidence is used instead, consistent with the documented TN TOC limitation that level-3 topic nodes are not independently page-anchored.

same_page_merge_resolutions.A.S01: Same-page merge of three real printed headings ('Acromyms', 'Overview of Anesthesia', 'Preoperative Assessment', all indexed to TN page A2 / pdf 56) confirmed via raw OCR of the TOC page (0055.json) and body pages (0056.json, 0057.json, 0058.json). Body-heading search additionally found that two of A.S01's three topic children ('Preoperative Investigations', 'American Society of Anesthesiology Classification') are physically printed on pdf page 58 (TN A4, within the nominal A.S02 range) rather than on pdf 56-57 as the TOC node's own declared A2-A3 range would suggest - a genuine page-boundary content overflow, not a TOC-extraction artifact. Split into SU-A-01 (Acronyms), SU-A-02 (Overview of Anesthesia), SU-A-03 (Preoperative Assessment, with its pdf_page_range tightened to [56,58] per the body-confirmed span).
same_page_merge_resolutions.A.S06: Same-page merge of 'Maintenance' + 'Extubation' + 'Complications of Extubation' (all indexed to TN page A20 / pdf 74). Raw OCR of body page 0074.json shows the true printed structure differs from the TOC's implied three-way split: 'Maintenance' and 'Complications of Extubation' ARE both genuine, independently-bolded body headings, but 'Extubation' is NOT - its criteria/procedure content is nested, unlabeled, inside the 'Maintenance' heading's own bullet list. A.S06 has zero topic children in toc_inventory.json, so both resolved study units (SU-A-20: Maintenance+Extubation; SU-A-21: Complications of Extubation) necessarily cite the same parent node A.S06 as their source, per protocol guidance for a merged node with no finer-grained children to redistribute across.

study_units.title: Acronyms (Chapter Glossary)
study_units.structural_rationale: Toronto Notes' own chapter-opening acronym glossary (pdf page 56, cols of abbreviations e.g. 'ABG', 'ASA', 'BMV'). Same-page-merge protocol applied: A.S01's merged_duplicate_headings field lists 'Overview of Anesthesia' and 'Preoperative Assessment' as headings absorbed into this node because all three share the printed TOC page label A2 (pdf 56). Raw OCR of the TOC page (derived/toronto-notes-2025/ocr/pages/0055.json) confirms three separate printed entries all indexed to A2: 'Acromyms', 'Overview of Anesthesia', 'Preoperative Assessment'. Raw OCR of the body page (0056.json) confirms the Acronyms table occupies the top of pdf page 56, immediately followed by a distinct 'Overview of Anesthesia' heading. This unit represents ONLY the Acronyms portion; the other two resolved headings are SU-A-02 and SU-A-03.

study_units.title: Overview of Anesthesia
source_hierarchy_path: A.S01 (Acromyms) [same-page merge resolution: Overview of Anesthesia portion]
study_units.structural_rationale: Second of the three headings resolved from the A.S01 same-page merge (see SU-A-01). Raw OCR of body page 0056.json confirms a distinct 'Overview of Anesthesia' heading directly beneath the acronym table, containing the definition of anesthesia ('a collection of changes contributing to lack of sensation/perception...') and a three-column table (Preoperative / Preoperative-Intraoperative / Postoperative) listing the phases of anesthetic care (assessment, optimization, airway management, monitors, induction, maintenance, emergence, extubation, disposition, pain management). This is purely orientational/definitional content that frames the rest of the chapter; it has no disease-specific testable competency of its own.

study_units.title: Preoperative Assessment (History, Investigations, ASA Classification)
source_hierarchy_path: A.S01 (Acromyms) [same-page merge resolution: Preoperative Assessment portion]
study_units.structural_rationale: Third of the three headings resolved from the A.S01 same-page merge (see SU-A-01). Raw OCR of body page 0056.json confirms 'Preoperative Assessment' as a distinct heading (Purpose: identify concerns, allay fears, arrange investigations, 'plan and consent for anesthetic techniques'), immediately followed by its first child topic 'History and Physical' (confirmed heading, content spans pdf 56-57: History checklist, then 'Physical Exam' sub-heading on pdf 57 covering airway assessment - Mallampati, 3-3-2 rule, LEMON/BONES mnemonics). The other two TOC topic children of this section, 'Preoperative Investigations' and 'American Society of Anesthesiology Classification', are NOT found as body headings on pdf 56-57 despite the TOC node's declared A2-A3 range; independent body-heading search (per same-page-merge protocol step 3) located both headings verbatim on pdf page 58 (TN A4), printed immediately before the 'Preoperative Optimization' section begins on the same page. This is a genuine page-boundary content overflow (the printed book's two-column layout runs this subsection's text onto the next TOC-indexed page), not a TOC-extraction merge artifact - so per protocol step 4 the unit's pdf_page_range is tightened to [56,58] to reflect the body-confirmed span rather than the TOC node's nominal A2-A3 declaration. All four resolved/topic components (assessment purpose+consent, Hx&PE, investigations, ASA-PS classification) are combined into one study unit because they are the sequential, inseparable steps of a single clinical process (preoperative assessment) explicitly named as such by Toronto Notes' own 'Preoperative Assessment' heading.

study_units.title: Preoperative Medications and Fasting Guidelines
study_units.structural_rationale: A.S02's own heading has independent content confirmed on pdf 58 ('in general, prior to elective surgery: fluid/electrolyte correction, comorbidity optimization, medication adjustment') immediately preceding its first child topic 'Medications' (confirmed heading, pdf 58, continuing onto pdf 59 with herbal-supplement and insulin/steroid adjustment bullets). 'Fasting Guidelines' is confirmed as its own heading on pdf 59 (Canadian Anesthesiologists' Society fasting-duration table). Grouped together as the two 'universal, applies-to-every-patient' preoperative optimization steps, distinct from the comorbidity-specific optimization topics in SU-A-05/06.

study_units.title: Preoperative Cardiopulmonary and Airway-Risk Optimization
study_units.structural_rationale: Five of A.S02's nine topic children, grouped because they share one clinical skill (perioperative risk stratification and optimization by comorbidity) and one shared physiologic theme (airway/cardiopulmonary risk). 'Hypertension' and 'Coronary Artery Disease' headings are confirmed on pdf 59 (BP threshold, ACC/AHA 60-day post-MI rule). 'Aspiration' is confirmed as its own heading on pdf 60 (risk-factor list + RSI cross-reference). 'Respiratory Diseases' and 'Obesity and Obstructive Sleep Apnea' fall in the same pdf 59-60 span per the TOC node's own declared bounds for A.S02 (end_pdf_page 60) but their exact heading position was not independently re-verified line-by-line; bounded confidently within [59,60] by the confirmed neighbors on both sides (Fasting Guidelines before, Hematological Disorders after).

study_units.title: Preoperative Hematologic and Endocrine Optimization
study_units.structural_rationale: Remaining two topic children of A.S02, both confirmed as headings on pdf 60 (Hematological Disorders: anemia/coagulopathy work-up and reversal-agent list; Endocrine Disorders: DM type/control/end-organ assessment). Grouped separately from SU-A-05 because they represent a distinct optimization skill (lab-based/metabolic risk correction) rather than airway/cardiopulmonary risk.

study_units.title: Patient Monitoring (Intraoperative Standards)
study_units.structural_rationale: This heading has NO corresponding node anywhere in toc_inventory.json's 59 chapter-A nodes - unlike the A.S01/A.S06 merges (which have an existing over-loaded node to split), the TOC-extraction pipeline dropped this heading entirely. research/tn2025/unresolved_headings.json records it as chapter_code 'A', heading_candidate 'Monitoring', source_pdf_page 55 (the TOC page), status UNRESOLVED, with search window pdf 58-66 checked and no match found at the pipeline's 0.87 similarity threshold. Independent resolution per the same-page-merge protocol's body-heading-search procedure: raw OCR of pdf page 61 (derived/toronto-notes-2025/ocr/pages/0061.json) shows the page opens with 'Canadian Guidelines to the Practice of Anesthesia and Patient Monitoring' as a heading, followed by 'Routine Monitors for All Cases' and 'Elements to Monitor' sub-headings, and is immediately followed on the SAME page by 'Airway Management' / 'Airway Anatomy' (which IS the confirmed body_line for node A.S03, extraction_method BODY_HEADING_CONFIRMATION, matched_body_line 'Airway Management'). This confirms the TOC's abbreviated index entry 'Monitoring...A7' refers to this longer printed heading, and explains why the automated pipeline's exact-string search for 'Monitoring' failed similarity threshold (the printed heading is 9 words, not the single word indexed). Represented as its own study unit sourced from a synthetic id (no real node exists to cite) since it is thematically distinct (intraoperative monitoring standards/equipment) from the airway content that follows it on the same page.

source_hierarchy_path: A.S06 (Maintenance) [same-page merge resolution: Maintenance + Extubation portion]

Raw OCR of body page 0074.json confirms the actual printed heading structure: a bold 'Maintenance' heading (general-anesthesia maintenance via volatile/IV agents + muscle relaxants) whose own bullet list continues directly into extubation-readiness criteria (patency, protection, spontaneous ventilation) and the extubation procedure itself - i.e., the TOC's separately-listed 'Extubation' entry does NOT correspond to its own independently-bolded body heading; its content is nested, unlabeled, inside the 'Maintenance' block. This study unit therefore represents both the TOC's 'Maintenance' and 'Extubation' entries together, matching the actual printed structure rather than inventing a heading split the source text does not contain (per protocol step 6: never infer a split heading not supported by the source).
